record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.context_brief: Equations for Hurwitz curves of genus 14 and 17
record.original_question: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a Hurwitz curve of genus g is a curve with exactly 84(g-1) automorphisms. Compute explicit equations for the Hurwitz curves of genus 14, and if possible for the Hurwitz curves of genus 17.

evidence.quote: A Hurwitz curve is a genus g curve, defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, which has 84(g - 1) automorphisms.
Problem 7. Compute equations for the Hurwitz curves of genus 14, and possibly 17.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. A smooth projective curve C of genus g ≥ 2 over k is called a Hurwitz curve if its automorphism group Aut(C) has order exactly 84(g − 1), which is the maximum possible by the Hurwitz bound.

(a) Determine explicit polynomial equations (for instance, equations cutting out the canonical embedding in projective space) defining each Hurwitz curve of genus 14 over k.

(b) If possible, determine explicit polynomial equations defining each Hurwitz curve of genus 17 over k.
artifact.category_tag: Hurwitz curves / algebraic curves with maximal automorphism group
artifact.status_search_result: A 2012 preprint by Bouw, Wewers and others titled "A canonical curve of genus 17" computes equations for a Hurwitz curve of genus 17 and shows that the canonical ideal of any Hurwitz curve of genus 14 or 17 is generated by quadrics. Equations for the genus 17 case have therefore been given, but a complete, explicit description of equations for all three Hurwitz curves of genus 14 does not appear to be settled in the literature.

status_evidence.title: A canonical curve of genus 17 (arXiv:1205.1567)
status_evidence.snippet: We compute equations for a Hurwitz curve of genus 17 and we conclude that the canonical ideal of any Hurwitz curve of genus 14 or 17 is generated by quadrics.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit equations for a Hurwitz curve of genus 17 have been computed; structural result on the canonical ideal in genus 14 is known, but full explicit equations in genus 14 are not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Hurwitz surface - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: At genus 14 there are three Hurwitz surfaces with automorphism group of order 1092; the only Hurwitz curves with classically known explicit equations are Klein's quartic and the Macbeath curve.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit equations for Hurwitz curves of genus 14 are not classically available; multiple Hurwitz curves exist in genus 14.
